The Qur'anic phrase: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah﴾

Some scholars said: He concealed His unseen knowledge from creation, and no one has been informed of it, so that none of His servants would feel secure from His plan (makr). It was also said that this verse was revealed concerning the polytheists when they asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the Hour (qiyamah).

The word "man" (من) is in the nominative case (raf'), and the meaning is: "Say: No one knows the unseen except Allah." The word "Allah" is a substitution (badal, apposition) for "man," as stated by al-Zajjaj.

Al-Farra' said: The word after "illa" (except) is in the nominative because what precedes it is a negation (juhd), as in your saying: "No one went except your father." The meaning is the same. Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever reads it in the accusative (nasb) treats it as an exception (istithna'), meaning in the speech.

Al-Nahhas said: I heard him (al-Zajjaj) use this verse as an argument against someone who believed an astrologer (munajjim), and he said: "I fear that he will disbelieve because of this verse." I say: This has already been discussed fully in Surat al-An'am [[See vol. 7, p. 1 and following, printed edition first or second.]]. 

Aisha said: Whoever claims that Muhammad knows what will happen tomorrow has committed a great slander against Allah, and Allah the Exalted says: "Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah." Muslim recorded it.

It is narrated that an astrologer entered upon al-Hajjaj, and al-Hajjaj detained him. Then he took some pebbles and counted them, and said: "How many pebbles are in my hand?" The astrologer calculated and then said: "So-and-so," and he was correct. Then he (al-Hajjaj) detained him again, took some pebbles which he did not count, and said: "How many are in my hand?" The astrologer calculated and was wrong, then calculated again and was wrong. Then he said: "O Amir, I think you do not know their number." He said: "No." He said: "Then I am not correct." He (al-Hajjaj) said: "What is the difference?" He said: "You counted those, so they left the limit of the unseen, but these you did not count, so they are unseen. And: 'None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah.'" This has already been discussed in Surat Al 'Imran [[See vol. 4, p. 17, printed edition first or second.]], and all praise is due to Allah.

The Qur'anic phrase: ﴿Rather, their knowledge has been overtaken concerning the Hereafter﴾

This is the reading of most people, including Asim, Shayba, Nafi', Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i. Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Humayd read: "Bal adraka" (rather, he has comprehended), from al-idrak (attainment/comprehension). Ata' ibn Yasar, his brother Sulayman ibn Yasar and al-A'mash [[The other tafsir books do not mention al-A'mash in this reading. Perhaps this is another narration from him, different from the one mentioned earlier.]] read: "Bal iddarak" without hamza and with a shadda (doubled letter). Ibn Muhaysin read: "Bal a'adraka" as an interrogative (istifham). Ibn Abbas read: "Bala" with the letter ya' affirmed, "a'addaraka" with a hamza of cutting (qat') and a doubled dal followed by an alif. Al-Nahhas said: Its chain of transmission is sound; it is from the narration of Shu'ba, traced back to Ibn Abbas. Harun al-Qari claimed that the reading of Ubayy is "Bal tadarraka 'ilmuhum," and that the first reading and this last one have the same meaning, because the origin of "iddarak" is "tadarak": the dal was assimilated (idgham) into the ta', and an alif of connection (alif al-wasl) was brought in. As for its meaning, there are two opinions. One is that the meaning is: "Rather, their knowledge became complete in the Hereafter," because they saw everything they had been promised directly, so their knowledge of it became complete. The other is that the meaning is: "Rather, their knowledge followed one another today concerning the Hereafter, so some said it will happen and some said it will not happen."

The second reading has two opinions: One is that its meaning is "it was completed in the Hereafter," which is like the first. Mujahid said: Its meaning is that their knowledge will be attained in the Hereafter, and they will know it when they witness it, at a time when their knowledge will not benefit them, because they were deniers in this world. The other opinion is that it has the sense of denial (inkar), which is the view of Abu Ishaq. He cited as evidence for the soundness of this view that what follows it is: ﴿Rather, they are in doubt about it﴾... ﴿Rather, they are blind to it﴾, meaning their knowledge did not attain the knowledge of the Hereafter. It was also said: Rather, their knowledge went astray and disappeared concerning the Hereafter, so they have no knowledge of it.

The third reading: "Bal adraka," which has the same meaning as "bal iddarak." The form "ifta'ala" and the form "tafa'ala" may have the same meaning, and for this reason "izdawaju" was used when it meant "tazawaju" (they married each other).

The fourth reading: In it there is only one opinion, in which there is the sense of denial, as you say: "Did I fight you?!" So the meaning is: "He did not attain." On this reading the reading of Ibn Abbas goes back. Ibn Abbas said: "Bala iddaraka 'ilmuhum fil-akhirah," meaning: he did not attain. Al-Farra' said: This is a good opinion, as if he directed it toward mockery of those who deny the Resurrection, like your saying to a man whom you are denying: "Yes, by my life, you have indeed met the predecessors, and you narrate what I do not narrate," while you are denying him.

A seventh reading: "Bal iddaraka," with a fatha on the lam, shifting to the fatha because it is lighter. Something similar has been related from Qutrub regarding "qumi al-layl" (stand the night), where he shifted to the fatha. Likewise "bi' al-thawb" (sell the garment) and similar.

Al-Zamakhshari mentioned in his book that it was also read: "Bal a'a'adraka" with two hamzas, "bal aa'adraka" with an alif between them, "bala a'addaraka," "am tadarraka," "am addaraka." These are twelve readings. Then he began explaining the aspects of the readings and said: If you ask, what is the aspect of the reading "bal a'adraka" as an interrogative? I say: It is an interrogative in the form of denial of the attainment of their knowledge. Likewise for whoever reads "am addaraka" and "am tadarraka," because it is the "am" which has the meaning of "bal" and the hamza. As for whoever reads "bala a'addaraka" as an interrogative, its meaning is: "Yes, they perceive when they will be resurrected," then he denied their knowledge of its occurrence. And when he denied their knowledge of its occurrence, no perception of its time was attained for them, because knowledge of the time of an occurrence follows knowledge of the occurrence itself.

"Fil-akhirah" (in the Hereafter): concerning the matter of the Hereafter and its meaning.

﴿Rather, they are in doubt about it﴾: that is, in this world.

﴿Rather, they are blind to it﴾: that is, in their hearts. Its singular is 'amm (blind). It was also said: 'Amin, and its origin is 'amyun; the ya' was dropped because of the meeting of two unvocalized letters, and it was not permissible to vowel it because of the heaviness of the vowel upon it.

This is the reading of most people, including Asim, Shayba, Nafi', Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i. Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Humayd read: "Bal adraka" (rather, he has comprehended), from al-idrak (attainment/comprehension). Ata' ibn Yasar, his brother Sulayman ibn Yasar and al-A'mash [[The other tafsir books do not mention al-A'mash in this reading. Perhaps this is another narration from him, different from the one mentioned earlier.]] read: "Bal iddarak" without hamza and with a shadda (doubled letter). Ibn Muhaysin read: "Bal a'adraka" as an interrogative (istifham). Ibn Abbas read: "Bala" with the letter ya' affirmed, "a'addaraka" with a hamza of cutting (qat') and a doubled dal followed by an alif. Al-Nahhas said: Its chain of transmission is sound; it is from the narration of Shu'ba, traced back to Ibn Abbas. Harun al-Qari claimed that the reading of Ubayy is "Bal tadarraka 'ilmuhum," and that the first reading and this last one have the same meaning, because the origin of "iddarak" is "tadarak": the dal was assimilated (idgham) into the ta', and an alif of connection (alif al-wasl) was brought in. As for its meaning, there are two opinions. One is that the meaning is: "Rather, their knowledge became complete in the Hereafter," because they saw everything they had been promised directly, so their knowledge of it became complete. The other is that the meaning is: "Rather, their knowledge followed one another today concerning the Hereafter, so some said it will happen and some said it will not happen."

The second reading has two opinions: One is that its meaning is "it was completed in the Hereafter," which is like the first. Mujahid said: Its meaning is that their knowledge will be attained in the Hereafter, and they will know it when they witness it, at a time when their knowledge will not benefit them, because they were deniers in this world. The other opinion is that it has the sense of denial (inkar), which is the view of Abu Ishaq. He cited as evidence for the soundness of this view that what follows it is: ﴿Rather, they are in doubt about it﴾... ﴿Rather, they are blind to it﴾, meaning their knowledge did not attain the knowledge of the Hereafter. It was also said: Rather, their knowledge went astray and disappeared concerning the Hereafter, so they have no knowledge of it.

The third reading: "Bal adraka," which has the same meaning as "bal iddarak." The form "ifta'ala" and the form "tafa'ala" may have the same meaning, and for this reason "izdawaju" was used when it meant "tazawaju" (they married each other).

The fourth reading: In it there is only one opinion, in which there is the sense of denial, as you say: "Did I fight you?!" So the meaning is: "He did not attain." On this reading the reading of Ibn Abbas goes back. Ibn Abbas said: "Bala iddaraka 'ilmuhum fil-akhirah," meaning: he did not attain. Al-Farra' said: This is a good opinion, as if he directed it toward mockery of those who deny the Resurrection, like your saying to a man whom you are denying: "Yes, by my life, you have indeed met the predecessors, and you narrate what I do not narrate," while you are denying him.

A seventh reading: "Bal iddaraka," with a fatha on the lam, shifting to the fatha because it is lighter. Something similar has been related from Qutrub regarding "qumi al-layl" (stand the night), where he shifted to the fatha. Likewise "bi' al-thawb" (sell the garment) and similar.

Al-Zamakhshari mentioned in his book that it was also read: "Bal a'a'adraka" with two hamzas, "bal aa'adraka" with an alif between them, "bala a'addaraka," "am tadarraka," "am addaraka." These are twelve readings. Then he began explaining the aspects of the readings and said: If you ask, what is the aspect of the reading "bal a'adraka" as an interrogative? I say: It is an interrogative in the form of denial of the attainment of their knowledge. Likewise for whoever reads "am addaraka" and "am tadarraka," because it is the "am" which has the meaning of "bal" and the hamza. As for whoever reads "bala a'addaraka" as an interrogative, its meaning is: "Yes, they perceive when they will be resurrected," then he denied their knowledge of its occurrence. And when he denied their knowledge of its occurrence, no perception of its time was attained for them, because knowledge of the time of an occurrence follows knowledge of the occurrence itself.

"Fil-akhirah" (in the Hereafter): concerning the matter of the Hereafter and its meaning.

﴿Rather, they are in doubt about it﴾: that is, in this world.

﴿Rather, they are blind to it﴾: that is, in their hearts. Its singular is 'amm (blind). It was also said: 'Amin, and its origin is 'amyun; the ya' was dropped because of the meeting of two unvocalized letters, and it was not permissible to vowel it because of the heaviness of the vowel upon it.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 67–68:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾, meaning the polytheists of Makkah.

(Idha kunna turaban wa-aba'una a-inna [[Ibn 'Atiyyah said: (with an elongated alif). The same is in al-Bahr and Ruh al-Ma'ani.]] lamukhrajun) — thus Nafi' recites it here and in Surat al-'Ankabut. Abu 'Amr recited with two interrogatives, except that he eased the hamza. 'Asim and Hamzah also recited with two interrogatives, except that both of them made the two hamzas clear (fully pronounced). Everything we have mentioned applies equally to both surahs. Al-Kisa'i, Ibn 'Amir, Ruways and Ya'qub recited "a-idha" with two hamzas and "inna" with two nuns, as a statement, in this surah, and in Surat al-'Ankabut with two interrogatives. Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas said: the reading "Idha kunna turaban wa-aba'una a-innna lamukhrajun" (with two interrogatives) agrees with the script and is good. Abu Hatim opposed it, and the meaning of his words is: "idha" is not an interrogative, while "a-inna" is an interrogative and contains "inna"; so how can what is within the scope of the interrogative govern what precedes it?! How can what follows "inna" govern what precedes it?! How is "ghadan inna Zaydan kharij" permissible?! If there is an interrogative in it, it is even further away; and when this is questioned, it becomes problematic for what he mentioned. Abu Ja'far said: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Walid say: "We asked Abu al-'Abbas about a verse of the Qur'an that is difficult and problematic, which is the saying of God, the Exalted: 'And those who disbelieved said: Shall we show you a man who will inform you when you are completely torn apart that you will be in a new creation?' " He said: If "yunabbi'ukum" governs "idha", it would be impossible, because it does not inform them at that time; and if what follows "inna" governs it, the meaning is sound, but it would be an error in Arabic for what precedes "inna" to govern what follows it. This is a clear question; I have seen it raised in the surah in which it occurs. As for Abu 'Ubayd, he inclined to the reading of Nafi' and rejected those who combined two interrogatives, and he cited the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿Then if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?﴾ and the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿Then if you die, will they be the immortals?﴾. This rebuttal of Abu 'Amr, 'Asim, Hamzah, Talhah and al-A'raj entails nothing, and it does not resemble at all what came in the verse; the difference between them is that the condition and its answer are as one thing, and the meaning of ﴿Then if you die, will they be the immortals?﴾ is: "Then if you die, will they be made immortal?" A parallel to this is: "a-Zayd munTaliq?" but one does not say "a-Zayd a-munTaliq?", because they are as one thing. The verse is not like that, because the second is a complete sentence in itself, so the interrogative is suitable in it, whereas the first is a statement in which the interrogative is suitable. As for the one who omits the interrogative from the second and affirms it in the first, he recites "a-idha kunna turaban wa-aba'una inna" and omits it from the second, because the context contains evidence for it in the sense of denial.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed we were promised this, we and our fathers before; this is nothing but the fables of the ancients﴾. It has been mentioned in Surat al-Mu'minun [[See vol. 12, p. 145, first or second edition.]]. The prophets used to bring near the matter of the Resurrection, as an emphasis in warning, and everything that is coming is near.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 69–71:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth﴾, meaning: say to these disbelievers, "Travel" through the lands of al-Sham, al-Hijaz and Yemen.

(Then look) meaning with your hearts and your insight (how was the end of the criminals) who denied their messengers.

(And do not grieve over them) meaning over the disbelievers of Makkah if they do not believe, (and do not be in distress) in hardship (because of what they plot). It was revealed concerning the mockers who divided up the paths of Makkah, and their mention has already passed [[See vol. 10, p. 58, first or second edition.]]. It is also read as "fi dayq" with a kasra, and this has already been discussed at the end of "al-Nahl" [[See vol. 10, p. 203, first or second edition.]].

(And they say: When is this promise) meaning, when will the punishment come upon us for our denial, (if you are truthful)?

(And they say: When is this promise) meaning, when will the punishment come upon us for our denial, (if you are truthful)?

"Say: It may be that some of what you seek to hasten has drawn near to you (radifa lakum)." That is, it has come close and approached you. "Some of what you seek to hasten": that is, of the punishment, said Ibn 'Abbas. It is from radifahu, when one follows him and comes in his wake. The lam may have been added because the meaning is "has drawn near to you and approached you." Or it may be connected to the verbal noun. It was also said: its meaning is "with you." Ibn Shajara said: "it followed you." From this comes ridf (the one riding behind) of a woman, because he follows her from behind. From this is the saying of Abu Dhu'ayb:

"Blackness returned to whiteness on his temples... no welcome to the whiteness of grey hair when it followed."

Al-Jawhari said: "Ardafahu" is a dialectal form of "radifahu," like "tabi'ahu" and "atba'ahu" with the same meaning. Khuzayma ibn Malik ibn Nahd said:

"When al-Jawza' (Orion) followed al-Thurayya (the Pleiades), I suspected the household of Fatima the worst suspicions."

He means Fatima daughter of Yadhkur ibn 'Anaza, one of the two "al-Qarizun." Al-Farra' said: "radifa lakum" means "approached you," and for this reason He said "lakum." It was also said: radifahu and radifa lahu have the same meaning, so the lam is added for emphasis; this is also from al-Farra'. Just as you say naqadtuhu and naqadtu lahu, and kiltuhu and wazantuhu, and kiltu lahu and wazantu lahu, and similar. "Some of what you seek to hasten" of the punishment: that was the day of Badr. It was also said: the punishment of the grave.

(And indeed your Lord is full of bounty toward mankind) in delaying punishment and granting abundant provision, (but most of them do not give thanks) for His bounty and His blessings.

His saying, the Exalted: "And indeed your Lord knows what their breasts conceal" (tukinnu sudurahum), meaning what their breasts hide, "and what they reveal" (yu'linun), what they display in affairs. Ibn Muhaysin and Humayd recited "ma takunnu," from kanantu al-shay' when I concealed it here. In al-Qasas its implied sense is: "what their breasts conceal against it," as if the pronoun in the breasts were a covering body. Whoever recites "tukinnu" is the familiar form, from akננtu al-shay' when you hide it within yourself.

His saying, the Exalted: "And there is no hidden thing in the heaven and the earth but that it is in a clear Book." Al-Hasan said: the hidden thing here is the Resurrection. It was also said: what is hidden from them of the punishment of heaven and earth, related by al-Naqqash. Ibn Shajara said: the hidden thing here is everything that Allah the Exalted has concealed from His creation and kept hidden from them, and this is general. The ta' marbuta entered "ghaibah" to indicate the collective, meaning: there is no hidden matter from the creation but that Allah knows it and has recorded it in the Mother of the Book with Him, so how could what these people conceal and what they declare be hidden from Him. It was also said: every thing that is recorded in the Mother of the Book He brings forth at its appointed term, so what they seek to hasten of the punishment has a set term from which it cannot be delayed or advanced. "The Book" is the Preserved Tablet, in which Allah recorded what He willed, so that He may inform whomever He wills of His angels.

Then he said: "Indeed they now know that what I used to tell them is the truth." Then ['A'ishah] recited [[i.e., 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] "Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear," until she recited the verse.

This verse has been opposed by the story of Badr, by the greeting upon graves, by what has been transmitted about the spirits being at the edges of graves at certain times, and by the report that the dead hear the sound of sandals when people turn away from them, and other such things. For if the dead did not hear, they would not be greeted. This is clear, and we have explained it in the book "al-Tadhkirah."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nor can you guide the blind away from their misguidance﴾, i.e., their disbelief; that is, it is not within your power to create faith in their hearts. Hamzah read: "wa ma anta tahdi al-'umya 'an dalalatihim," like His saying: "Will you then guide the blind?" The rest read: "bi-hadi al-'umy," and this is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim; and in "al-Rum" it is similar. All of them stopped on "bi-hadi" with the ya' in this surah, and without a ya' in "al-Rum," following the Mushaf, except Ya'qub, who stopped on the ya' in both. Al-Farra' and Abu Hatim permitted: "wa ma anta bi-hadi al-'umy," which is the original form. In the reading of 'Abdullah: "wa ma an tahdiya al-'umy."

(Only he who) (in tusmi') means: what you cause to hear.

(Only he who believes in Our signs) Ibn 'Abbas said: i.e., only those whom I created for happiness, for they are sincere in monotheism.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 76–81:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an narrates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they differ﴾. This was because they differed over many matters, to the point that some of them cursed others, and so it was revealed. The meaning is: this Qur'an explains to them what they differed about, if they were to act upon it, and that includes what they distorted from the Torah and the Gospel, and the rulings that were lost from their books.

(And indeed it) meaning the Qur'an (is guidance and mercy for the believers). He specified the believers because they are the ones who benefit from it.

(Indeed, your Lord will judge between them by His ruling) i.e., He will judge between the Children of Israel concerning what they differed over, on the Day of Judgment, so He will reward the righteous and the wrongdoer. It was also said: He will judge between them in this world, and will manifest what they distorted.

(And He is the Mighty) the Invincible, the Overpowering, whose command cannot be repelled, (the All-Knowing) to whom nothing is hidden.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So put your trust in Allah﴾, i.e., entrust your affair to Him and rely upon Him, for He is your helper.

(Indeed, you are upon the manifest truth) i.e., the evident. It was also said: the one who makes clear the correct way to whoever reflects upon it.

(Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear) meaning the disbelievers, because of their refusal to reflect; they are like the dead, having neither perception nor intellect. It was also said: this refers to those whom he knew would not believe.

(Nor can you make the deaf hear the call) meaning the disbelievers who are like the deaf in refusing to accept admonitions; when they are called to good, they turn away and withdraw as if they did not hear. Its parallel is "deaf, dumb, and blind," as has preceded. Ibn Muhaysin, Humayd, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Abbas on the authority of Abu 'Amr read "wa la yasma'u" with a fathah on the ya' and the mim, "al-summu" in the nominative as the subject. The rest read "tusmi'" as the imperfect of asma'ta, "al-samma" in the accusative. Issue: 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, argued against the claim that the Prophet ﷺ made the dead of Badr hear, using this verse. She examined the matter by rational analogy and held to this verse. However, it is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "You are no more able to hear than they are." Ibn 'Atiyyah said: It seems that the story of Badr was a breach of custom for Muhammad ﷺ, in that Allah returned to them a perception by which they heard his speech; and if not for the reports of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about their hearing, we would have interpreted his calling to them as a rebuke to the remaining disbelievers, and as a means of healing the hearts of the believers. I say: al-Bukhari, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated: "Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to me, having heard Rawh ibn 'Ubadah say: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Anas ibn Malik related to us from Abu Talhah that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ ordered on the day of Badr that twenty-four men of the chiefs of Quraysh be thrown into a foul well among the wells of Badr. Whenever he prevailed over a people, he would remain on the battlefield for three nights. On the third day at Badr, he ordered his mount to be saddled, then walked, and his companions followed him. They said: We do not think he is setting out except for some need, until he stood at the edge of the well and began calling them by their names and their fathers' names: 'O so-and-so son of so-and-so, and O so-and-so son of so-and-so, would it please you that you had obeyed Allah and His Messenger? For we have found what our Lord promised us to be true; have you found what your Lord promised to be true?' Qatadah said: 'Umar said: O Messenger of Allah! Do you speak to bodies that have no souls?' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are no more able to hear what I say than they are.'" Qatadah said: "Allah brought them back to life until He let them hear His words, as a rebuke, a humiliation, a punishment, a regret, and remorse." Muslim also recorded it. Al-Bukhari said: "Uthman related to us, saying: 'Abdah related to us from Hisham, from his father, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Prophet ﷺ stood over the well of Badr and said: "Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?" Then he said: "Indeed they now know that what I used to tell them is the truth." Then ['A'ishah] recited [[i.e., 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] "Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear," until she recited the verse.

This verse has been opposed by the story of Badr, by the greeting upon graves, by what has been transmitted about the spirits being at the edges of graves at certain times, and by the report that the dead hear the sound of sandals when people turn away from them, and other such things. For if the dead did not hear, they would not be greeted. This is clear, and we have explained it in the book "al-Tadhkirah."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nor can you guide the blind away from their misguidance﴾, i.e., their disbelief; that is, it is not within your power to create faith in their hearts. Hamzah read: "wa ma anta tahdi al-'umya 'an dalalatihim," like His saying: "Will you then guide the blind?" The rest read: "bi-hadi al-'umy," and this is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim; and in "al-Rum" it is similar. All of them stopped on "bi-hadi" with the ya' in this surah, and without a ya' in "al-Rum," following the Mushaf, except Ya'qub, who stopped on the ya' in both. Al-Farra' and Abu Hatim permitted: "wa ma anta bi-hadi al-'umy," which is the original form. In the reading of 'Abdullah: "wa ma an tahdiya al-'umy."

(Only he who) (in tusmi') means: what you cause to hear.

(Only he who believes in Our signs) Ibn 'Abbas said: i.e., only those whom I created for happiness, for they are sincere in monotheism.

The Almighty said: ﴿And when the word is fulfilled against them, We shall bring forth for them a beast from the earth, which will speak to them﴾. Scholars differed over the meaning of "the word is fulfilled" (waqa'a al-qawl) and over the beast. It was said: the meaning of "the word is fulfilled against them" is that wrath becomes due against them. This was said by Qatadah. Mujahid said: that is, the word is confirmed against them that they will not believe. Ibn Umar and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: when they do not enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, displeasure becomes due against them. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: the fulfilment of the word occurs through the death of the scholars, the disappearance of knowledge, and the lifting of the Qur'an. He said: "Recite the Qur'an abundantly before it is lifted." They said: "These copies (mushaf) will be lifted, so what about what is in the hearts of men?" He said: "It will be carried away by night, and in the morning they will be empty of it. They will forget 'there is no god but Allah,' and they will fall into the speech of the Jahiliyyah and its poetry. That is when the word is fulfilled against them."

I say: Abu Bakr al-Bazzar transmitted it with a chain: he said, "Abdullah ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Majid ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from a son of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from his father, that he said: 'Visit this House (the Ka'bah) abundantly before it is lifted and people forget its place, and recite the Qur'an abundantly before it is lifted.' They said: 'O Abu Abd al-Rahman, these copies will be lifted, so what about what is in the hearts of men?' He said: 'They will rise in the morning and say: "We used to speak a speech and say a saying," and they will return to the poetry and tales of the Jahiliyyah. That is when the word is fulfilled against them.'"

It was also said: the "word" is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But the word from Me is true: I will surely fill Hell﴾. So the fulfilment of the word is the obligation of punishment upon these people. When they reach a state in which their repentance is no longer accepted and no believing child is born to them, then the Hour will come. This was mentioned by al-Qushayri.

A sixth view: Hafsah bint Sirin said: I asked Abu al-Aliyah about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "And when the word is fulfilled against them, We shall bring forth for them a beast from the earth, which will speak to them." He said: Allah revealed to Nuh: "He will not believe, of your people, except those who have already believed." It was as if there had been a covering over my face, and it was uncovered.

Al-Nahhas said: This is a fine answer, because people are being tested and postponed, since among them are believers and righteous people, and whoever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows will believe and repent. For this reason they are granted respite, and we are commanded to take the jizyah. When this ceases, the word becomes due against them, and they become like the people of Nuh when Allah, the Exalted, said: "He will not believe, of your people, except those who have already believed."

I say: On careful reflection, all the sayings return to one meaning. The evidence for this is the end of the verse: ﴿that the people were not certain of Our signs﴾. It is also read with the hamzah of "anna" (that) vowelled with a fatha, and it will come.

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three things, when they come forth, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earn good through its faith: the rising of the sun from its west, the Dajjal, and the beast of the earth." This has already passed.

Scholars differed greatly over identifying this beast, its description, and where it will emerge. We have mentioned this in the book al-Tadhkirah, and we will mention it here in full, if Allah the Exalted wills. The first of the sayings is that it is the young camel (fasil) of the she-camel of Salih, and this is the most sound of them, Allah knows best, because of what Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi mentioned in his Musnad from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the beast and said: "It has three emergences over time. It will emerge in the farthest part of the desert, and its mention will not enter the town, meaning Makkah. Then it will remain hidden for a long time. Then it will emerge in another emergence, less than that, and its mention will spread in the desert and enter the town, meaning Makkah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then, while people are in the most sacred of the mosques before Allah, the best of them and the most honoured by Allah, the Sacred Mosque, it will come upon them unexpectedly, and it will be roaring between the Corner and the Station (Maqam), shaking the dust from its head. The people will scatter from it in every direction, but a band of believers will stand firm, knowing that they cannot escape Allah. It will then begin with them and make their faces shine until it makes them like a shining star, and it will turn away in the earth. No pursuer will overtake it, and no fugitive will escape it, to the extent that a man will seek refuge from it in prayer, and it will come to him from behind and say: 'O so-and-so, now you pray!' Then it will turn to him and mark him on his face, and then it will depart. People will share in wealth, and will be reconciled in the cities. The believer will be recognised from the disbeliever, to the extent that the believer will say: 'O disbeliever, pay me my right.'"

The point of evidence in this hadith that it is the young camel is the phrase "and it is roaring (targhu)," and roaring (rughaa') belongs only to camels. This is because when the she-camel was slain, the young camel fled, and a rock opened for it, and it entered into its inside, and then it closed upon it, and it remains within until it emerges by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

It was also reported that it is a hairy, downy creature with legs whose length is sixty cubits. It is said that it is al-Jassasah, and this is the saying of Abdullah ibn Umar. It was reported from Ibn Umar that it is in the form of the children of Adam, and it is in the clouds while its legs are on the earth. It was also reported that it was assembled from the form of every animal.

Al-Mawardi and al-Tha'labi mentioned: its head is the head of a bull, its eye is the eye of a pig, its ear is the ear of an elephant, its horn is the horn of a stag, its neck is the neck of an ostrich, its chest is the chest of a lion, its colour is the colour of a leopard, its flank is the flank of a cat, its tail is the tail of a ram, and its legs are the legs of a camel, with twelve cubits between each joint and joint. (Al-Zamakhshari said: by the cubit of Adam, peace be upon him.) Along with it will come the staff of Musa and the ring of Sulayman, peace be upon them both. It will strike the face of the believer with the staff of Musa, leaving a white mark, and his face will become white. It will strike the face of the disbeliever with the ring of Sulayman, peace be upon him, and his face will become black. This was said by Ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both.

In the book of al-Naqqash, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: the beast is the serpent that was perched on the wall of the Ka'bah, which the eagle snatched away when the Quraysh wanted to rebuild the Ka'bah.

Al-Mawardi related from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was asked about the beast, and he said: "By Allah, it has no tail, but it has a beard." Al-Mawardi said: In this statement of his there is an indication that it is of mankind, even though he did not state it explicitly.

I say: For this reason, Allah knows best, some of the later exegetes said: The closer view is that this beast is a speaking human being who debates the people of innovation and disbelief and argues with them so that they are silenced, so that whoever perishes perishes by clear evidence, and whoever lives lives by clear evidence. Our shaykh, the Imam Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Umar al-Qurtubi, said in his book al-Mufhim: The reason this speaker held the view that it is closer is His saying, the Exalted: "it will speak to them." On this view, there is no extraordinary sign specific to this beast, and it would not be among the ten signs mentioned in the hadith, because the existence of debaters and those who argue against the people of innovation is common, so there is no sign specific to it, and it should not be mentioned with the ten. Its unique existence is also lifted when the word is fulfilled. Moreover, it involves a departure from naming this virtuous, learned debater, whom the people of the earth should call a human, a scholar, or an imam, by the name of a beast. This is a departure from the custom of eloquent speakers and from the honouring of scholars, and it is not the practice of sensible people. So the better view is what the people of tafsir have said, and Allah knows best the realities of matters.

I say: The difficulty concerning this beast has been removed by what we have mentioned from the hadith of Hudhayfah, so let it be relied upon. It has been disputed from which place it will emerge. Abdullah ibn Umar said: It will emerge from Mount Safa in Makkah, splitting open, and it will come out of it. Abdullah ibn Amr said something similar and said: "If I wished to place my foot upon the place of its emergence, I would do so." It was also reported in a report from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The earth will split open for the beast, while Isa, peace be upon him, is circling the House, and with him are the Muslims from the direction of al-Masa'. It will emerge from al-Safa and will mark between the eyes of the believer, 'this is a believer,' with a mark like a shining star, and will mark between the eyes of the disbeliever with a black spot, 'this is a disbeliever.'" It is also mentioned in the report that it has fur and feathers, as al-Mahdawi mentioned.

From Ibn Abbas: it will emerge from a mountain pass, its head touching the clouds while its feet are still in the earth, not yet emerged. It will come out with the staff of Musa and the ring of Sulayman, peace be upon them both.

From Hudhayfah: it will emerge three times: one emergence in some of the deserts, then it will remain hidden; and an emergence in the towns, where the rulers will fight one another until much blood is shed; and an emergence from the greatest, most honoured, noblest and most excellent of the mosques. Al-Zamakhshari said: it will emerge from between the Corner, opposite the house of Banu Makhzum, on the right of one leaving the mosque. Some people will flee, and some will stand watching.

It was reported from Qatadah that it will emerge in Tihamah. It was also reported that it will emerge from the mosque of Kufah, from the place where the oven of Nuh, peace be upon him, boiled over. It was also said: from the land of al-Ta'if. Abu Qabil said: Abdullah ibn Amr struck the land of al-Ta'if with his foot and said: "From here the beast will emerge which speaks to the people." It was also said: from some valleys of Tihamah, said by Ibn Abbas. It was said: from a rock in the valley of Ajyad, said by Abdullah ibn Amr. It was said: from the Sea of Sodom (Sadum), said by Wahb ibn Munabbih. Al-Mawardi mentioned these last three sayings in his book.

Al-Baghawi Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz mentioned: Ali ibn al-Ja'd narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq al-Raqqashi al-Aghar (about whom Yahya ibn Ma'in was asked, and he said: "trustworthy"), from Atiyyah al-Awfi, from Ibn Umar, who said: "The beast will emerge from a crack in the Ka'bah, running like a horse for three days, and a third of it will not emerge."

I say: These are the sayings of the Companions and the Successor regarding the emergence of the beast and its description. They refute the view of those exegetes who said that the beast is merely a speaking human being who debates the people of innovation and disbelief. Abu Umamah narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The beast will emerge and mark people on their noses." This was mentioned by al-Mawardi.

"تُكَلِّمُهُمْ" with a ḍammah

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 27, verses 82–86 (part 2 of 2):

The reading of the common readers (qira'ah, recitation) is *tukallimuhum* (تُكَلِّمُهُمْ) with a *tā'* and a doubled *lām* that is karsa, from *al-kalam* (speech). Evidence for it is the reading of Ubayy, "tunabbi'uhum" (تُنَبِّئُهُمْ). Al-Suddi said: "It speaks to them about the falsehood of all religions other than the religion of Islam." It was also said: "It speaks to them with what distresses them." It was also said: "It speaks to them in an eloquent tongue, saying in a voice that is heard by those near and far: *'Inna al-nasa kanu bi-ayatina la yuqinun'* (that people did not have certainty in Our signs)," meaning in My coming out, because its coming out is one of the signs. And it says: "Surely the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers."

Abu Zur'ah, Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Abu Raja' read *takulimuhum* (تَكْلِمُهُمْ) with a fatha on the *tā'*, from *al-kalm*, which is the wound. Ikrimah said: that is, it brands them. Abu al-Jawza' said: I asked Ibn Abbas about this verse, "*tukallimuhum*" or "*takulimuhum*"? He said: "By Allah, it is both: it speaks to the believer, and it wounds the disbeliever and the wicked," that is, it wounds him. Abu Hatim said: "*tukallimuhum*" is like saying "*tujarrihuhum*" (it wounds them); he holds that it is an intensive form of "*takulimuhum*."

*Anna al-nasa kanu bi-ayatina la yuqinun* (أَنَّ النَّاسَ كانُوا بِآياتِنا لَا يُوقِنُونَ): The Kufans, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Yahya read *anna* (أَنَّ) with a fatha. The people of the two Holy Cities, the people of Syria and the people of Basra read *inna* (إِنَّ) with a kasra on the hamza. Al-Nahhas said: regarding the fatha-form there are two opinions, and likewise the kasra-form. Al-Akhfash said: the meaning is *bi-anna* (بِأَنَّ), and Ibn Mas'ud also read *bi-anna*. Abu Ubaydah said: its position is in the accusative by the verb falling upon it, meaning: it informs them that the people [...]. Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' read *inna al-nas* (إِنَّ النَّاسَ) with a kasra, as a new sentence (isti'naf). Al-Akhfash said: it has the meaning of "you say, *inna al-nas*," meaning the disbelievers. "*Bi-ayatina la yuqinun*" means: with the Qur'an and with Muhammad (ﷺ), and that is when Allah will not accept faith from a disbeliever, and only believers and disbelievers remain in Allah's knowledge before its coming out. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And on the Day when We shall gather from every nation a troop﴾: that is, a group and a company.

(*Min man yukadhdhibu bi-ayatina*, "of those who deny Our signs"): meaning with the Qur'an and with Our clear indications that point to the truth.

(*Fahum yuza'un*, "then they will be driven"): that is, they will be pushed and driven to the place of reckoning. Al-Shammakh said:

"How many a host of a massive army have we driven back,
and how many a chief, vigorous and sharp, have we bestowed."

Qatadah said: "*yuza'un*" means that their first is held back until their last joins them.

(*Hatta idha ja'u qala*, "until, when they come, He will say"): that is, Allah says: (*Akadhdhabtum bi-ayati*, "Did you deny My signs") which I sent down upon My messengers, and the signs which I established as proof of My oneness?

(*Wa lam tuhituu biha 'ilman*, "while you did not encompass them in knowledge"): that is, you did not know their falsehood so that you would turn away from them; rather, you denied them in ignorance, without seeking evidence.

(*Amma dha kuntum ta'maluna*, "or what were you doing?"): this is rebuke and reproach. That is: what were you doing when you did not investigate them and did not reflect on what is in them?

(*Wa waqa'a al-qawlu 'alayhim bima zalamu*, "and the word will fall upon them because of what they wronged"): that is, the punishment becomes due upon them because of their wrongdoing, that is, their polytheism.

(*Fahum la yantiqun*, "so they will not speak"): that is, they have no excuse and no proof. It was said: their mouths will be sealed so they do not speak. This is what most of the exegetes said.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they not see that We made the night for them to rest therein﴾: that is, that they may settle and sleep.

(*Wa al-nahara mubsiran*, "and the day as something to see by"): that is, it is seen by, for the pursuit of provision.

(*Inna fi dhalika la-ayatin li-qawmin yu'minun*, "Surely in that are signs for a people who believe"): in Allah. He mentioned the proof of His divinity and His power, meaning: have they not known the completeness of Our power so that they would believe?

The Almighty said: ﴿And when the word is fulfilled against them, We shall bring forth for them a beast from the earth, which will speak to them﴾. Scholars differed over the meaning of "the word is fulfilled" (waqa'a al-qawl) and over the beast. It was said: the meaning of "the word is fulfilled against them" is that wrath becomes due against them. This was said by Qatadah. Mujahid said: that is, the word is confirmed against them that they will not believe. Ibn Umar and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: when they do not enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, displeasure becomes due against them. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: the fulfilment of the word occurs through the death of the scholars, the disappearance of knowledge, and the lifting of the Qur'an. He said: "Recite the Qur'an abundantly before it is lifted." They said: "These copies (mushaf) will be lifted, so what about what is in the hearts of men?" He said: "It will be carried away by night, and in the morning they will be empty of it. They will forget 'there is no god but Allah,' and they will fall into the speech of the Jahiliyyah and its poetry. That is when the word is fulfilled against them."

I say: Abu Bakr al-Bazzar transmitted it with a chain: he said, "Abdullah ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Majid ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from a son of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from his father, that he said: 'Visit this House (the Ka'bah) abundantly before it is lifted and people forget its place, and recite the Qur'an abundantly before it is lifted.' They said: 'O Abu Abd al-Rahman, these copies will be lifted, so what about what is in the hearts of men?' He said: 'They will rise in the morning and say: "We used to speak a speech and say a saying," and they will return to the poetry and tales of the Jahiliyyah. That is when the word is fulfilled against them.'"

It was also said: the "word" is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But the word from Me is true: I will surely fill Hell﴾. So the fulfilment of the word is the obligation of punishment upon these people. When they reach a state in which their repentance is no longer accepted and no believing child is born to them, then the Hour will come. This was mentioned by al-Qushayri.

A sixth view: Hafsah bint Sirin said: I asked Abu al-Aliyah about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "And when the word is fulfilled against them, We shall bring forth for them a beast from the earth, which will speak to them." He said: Allah revealed to Nuh: "He will not believe, of your people, except those who have already believed." It was as if there had been a covering over my face, and it was uncovered.

Al-Nahhas said: This is a fine answer, because people are being tested and postponed, since among them are believers and righteous people, and whoever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows will believe and repent. For this reason they are granted respite, and we are commanded to take the jizyah. When this ceases, the word becomes due against them, and they become like the people of Nuh when Allah, the Exalted, said: "He will not believe, of your people, except those who have already believed."

I say: On careful reflection, all the sayings return to one meaning. The evidence for this is the end of the verse: ﴿that the people were not certain of Our signs﴾. It is also read with the hamzah of "anna" (that) vowelled with a fatha, and it will come.

Then it will emerge in another emergence, less than that, and its mention will spread in the desert and enter the town, meaning Makkah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then, while people are in the most sacred of the mosques before Allah, the best of them and the most honoured by Allah, the Sacred Mosque, it will come upon them unexpectedly, and it will be roaring between the Corner and the Station (Maqam), shaking the dust from its head. Abu Zur'ah, Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Abu Raja' read *takulimuhum* (تَكْلِمُهُمْ) with a fatha on the *tā'*, from *al-kalm*, which is the wound. Ikrimah said: that is, it brands them. "*Bi-ayatina la yuqinun*" means: with the Qur'an and with Muhammad (ﷺ), and that is when Allah will not accept faith from a disbeliever, and only believers and disbelievers remain in Allah's knowledge before its coming out. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And on the Day when We shall gather from every nation a troop﴾: that is, a group and a company.

(*Min man yukadhdhibu bi-ayatina*, "of those who deny Our signs"): meaning with the Qur'an and with Our clear indications that point to the truth.

(*Fahum yuza'un*, "then they will be driven"): that is, they will be pushed and driven to the place of reckoning. Al-Shammakh said:

"How many a host of a massive army have we driven back,
and how many a chief, vigorous and sharp, have we bestowed."

Qatadah said: "*yuza'un*" means that their first is held back until their last joins them.

(*Hatta idha ja'u qala*, "until, when they come, He will say"): that is, Allah says: (*Akadhdhabtum bi-ayati*, "Did you deny My signs") which I sent down upon My messengers, and the signs which I established as proof of My oneness?

(*Wa lam tuhituu biha 'ilman*, "while you did not encompass them in knowledge"): that is, you did not know their falsehood so that you would turn away from them; rather, you denied them in ignorance, without seeking evidence.

(*Amma dha kuntum ta'maluna*, "or what were you doing?"): this is rebuke and reproach. That is: what were you doing when you did not investigate them and did not reflect on what is in them?

(*Wa waqa'a al-qawlu 'alayhim bima zalamu*, "and the word will fall upon them because of what they wronged"): that is, the punishment becomes due upon them because of their wrongdoing, that is, their polytheism.

(*Fahum la yantiqun*, "so they will not speak"): that is, they have no excuse and no proof. It was said: their mouths will be sealed so they do not speak. This is what most of the exegetes said.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they not see that We made the night for them to rest therein﴾: that is, that they may settle and sleep.

(*Wa al-nahara mubsiran*, "and the day as something to see by"): that is, it is seen by, for the pursuit of provision.

Abu Ubaydah said: its position is in the accusative by the verb falling upon it, meaning: it informs them that the people [...]. Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' read *inna al-nas* (إِنَّ النَّاسَ) with a kasra, as a new sentence (isti'naf). Al-Akhfash said: it has the meaning of "you say, *inna al-nas*," meaning the disbelievers. "*Bi-ayatina la yuqinun*" means: with the Qur'an and with Muhammad (ﷺ), and that is when Allah will not accept faith from a disbeliever, and only believers and disbelievers remain in Allah's knowledge before its coming out. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And on the Day when We shall gather from every nation a troop﴾: that is, a group and a company.

(*Min man yukadhdhibu bi-ayatina*, "of those who deny Our signs"): meaning with the Qur'an and with Our clear indications that point to the truth.

(*Fahum yuza'un*, "then they will be driven"): that is, they will be pushed and driven to the place of reckoning. Al-Shammakh said:

"How many a host of a massive army have we driven back,
and how many a chief, vigorous and sharp, have we bestowed."

Qatadah said: "*yuza'un*" means that their first is held back until their last joins them.

(*Hatta idha ja'u qala*, "until, when they come, He will say"): that is, Allah says: (*Akadhdhabtum bi-ayati*, "Did you deny My signs") which I sent down upon My messengers, and the signs which I established as proof of My oneness?

(*Wa lam tuhituu biha 'ilman*, "while you did not encompass them in knowledge"): that is, you did not know their falsehood so that you would turn away from them; rather, you denied them in ignorance, without seeking evidence.

(*Amma dha kuntum ta'maluna*, "or what were you doing?"): this is rebuke and reproach. That is: what were you doing when you did not investigate them and did not reflect on what is in them?

(*Wa waqa'a al-qawlu 'alayhim bima zalamu*, "and the word will fall upon them because of what they wronged"): that is, the punishment becomes due upon them because of their wrongdoing, that is, their polytheism.

(*Fahum la yantiqun*, "so they will not speak"): that is, they have no excuse and no proof. It was said: their mouths will be sealed so they do not speak. This is what most of the exegetes said.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they not see that We made the night for them to rest therein﴾: that is, that they may settle and sleep.

(*Wa al-nahara mubsiran*, "and the day as something to see by"): that is, it is seen by, for the pursuit of provision.

(*Inna fi dhalika la-ayatin li-qawmin yu'minun*, "Surely in that are signs for a people who believe"): in Allah. He mentioned the proof of His divinity and His power, meaning: have they not known the completeness of Our power so that they would believe?

The Almighty said: ﴿And when the word is fulfilled against them, We shall bring forth for them a beast from the earth, which will speak to them﴾. Scholars differed over the meaning of "the word is fulfilled" (waqa'a al-qawl) and over the beast. It was said: the meaning of "the word is fulfilled against them" is that wrath becomes due against them. This was said by Qatadah. Mujahid said: that is, the word is confirmed against them that they will not believe. Ibn Umar and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: when they do not enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, displeasure becomes due against them. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: the fulfilment of the word occurs through the death of the scholars, the disappearance of knowledge, and the lifting of the Qur'an. He said: "Recite the Qur'an abundantly before it is lifted." They said: "These copies (mushaf) will be lifted, so what about what is in the hearts of men?" He said: "It will be carried away by night, and in the morning they will be empty of it. They will forget 'there is no god but Allah,' and they will fall into the speech of the Jahiliyyah and its poetry. That is when the word is fulfilled against them."

I say: Abu Bakr al-Bazzar transmitted it with a chain: he said, "Abdullah ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Majid ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from a son of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from his father, that he said: 'Visit this House (the Ka'bah) abundantly before it is lifted and people forget its place, and recite the Qur'an abundantly before it is lifted.' They said: 'O Abu Abd al-Rahman, these copies will be lifted, so what about what is in the hearts of men?' He said: 'They will rise in the morning and say: "We used to speak a speech and say a saying," and they will return to the poetry and tales of the Jahiliyyah. That is when the word is fulfilled against them.'"

It was also said: the "word" is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But the word from Me is true: I will surely fill Hell﴾. So the fulfilment of the word is the obligation of punishment upon these people. When they reach a state in which their repentance is no longer accepted and no believing child is born to them, then the Hour will come. This was mentioned by al-Qushayri.

A sixth view: Hafsah bint Sirin said: I asked Abu al-Aliyah about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "And when the word is fulfilled against them, We shall bring forth for them a beast from the earth, which will speak to them." He said: Allah revealed to Nuh: "He will not believe, of your people, except those who have already believed." It was as if there had been a covering over my face, and it was uncovered.

Al-Nahhas said: This is a fine answer, because people are being tested and postponed, since among them are believers and righteous people, and whoever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows will believe and repent. For this reason they are granted respite, and we are commanded to take the jizyah. When this ceases, the word becomes due against them, and they become like the people of Nuh when Allah, the Exalted, said: "He will not believe, of your people, except those who have already believed."

I say: On careful reflection, all the sayings return to one meaning. The evidence for this is the end of the verse: ﴿that the people were not certain of Our signs﴾. It is also read with the hamzah of "anna" (that) vowelled with a fatha, and it will come.

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three things, when they come forth, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earn good through its faith: the rising of the sun from its west, the Dajjal, and the beast of the earth." This has already passed.

Scholars differed greatly over identifying this beast, its description, and where it will emerge. We have mentioned this in the book al-Tadhkirah, and we will mention it here in full, if Allah the Exalted wills. The first of the sayings is that it is the young camel (fasil) of the she-camel of Salih, and this is the most sound of them, Allah knows best, because of what Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi mentioned in his Musnad from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the beast and said: "It has three emergences over time. It will emerge in the farthest part of the desert, and its mention will not enter the town, meaning Makkah. Then it will remain hidden for a long time. Then it will emerge in another emergence, less than that, and its mention will spread in the desert and enter the town, meaning Makkah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then, while people are in the most sacred of the mosques before Allah, the best of them and the most honoured by Allah, the Sacred Mosque, it will come upon them unexpectedly, and it will be roaring between the Corner and the Station (Maqam), shaking the dust from its head. The people will scatter from it in every direction, but a band of believers will stand firm, knowing that they cannot escape Allah. It will then begin with them and make their faces shine until it makes them like a shining star, and it will turn away in the earth. No pursuer will overtake it, and no fugitive will escape it, to the extent that a man will seek refuge from it in prayer, and it will come to him from behind and say: 'O so-and-so, now you pray!' Then it will turn to him and mark him on his face, and then it will depart. People will share in wealth, and will be reconciled in the cities. The believer will be recognised from the disbeliever, to the extent that the believer will say: 'O disbeliever, pay me my right.'"

The point of evidence in this hadith that it is the young camel is the phrase "and it is roaring (targhu)," and roaring (rughaa') belongs only to camels. This is because when the she-camel was slain, the young camel fled, and a rock opened for it, and it entered into its inside, and then it closed upon it, and it remains within until it emerges by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

It was also reported that it is a hairy, downy creature with legs whose length is sixty cubits. It is said that it is al-Jassasah, and this is the saying of Abdullah ibn Umar. It was reported from Ibn Umar that it is in the form of the children of Adam, and it is in the clouds while its legs are on the earth. It was also reported that it was assembled from the form of every animal.

Al-Mawardi and al-Tha'labi mentioned: its head is the head of a bull, its eye is the eye of a pig, its ear is the ear of an elephant, its horn is the horn of a stag, its neck is the neck of an ostrich, its chest is the chest of a lion, its colour is the colour of a leopard, its flank is the flank of a cat, its tail is the tail of a ram, and its legs are the legs of a camel, with twelve cubits between each joint and joint. (Al-Zamakhshari said: by the cubit of Adam, peace be upon him.) Along with it will come the staff of Musa and the ring of Sulayman, peace be upon them both. It will strike the face of the believer with the staff of Musa, leaving a white mark, and his face will become white. It will strike the face of the disbeliever with the ring of Sulayman, peace be upon him, and his face will become black. This was said by Ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both.

In the book of al-Naqqash, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: the beast is the serpent that was perched on the wall of the Ka'bah, which the eagle snatched away when the Quraysh wanted to rebuild the Ka'bah.

Al-Mawardi said: In this statement of his there is an indication that it is of mankind, even though he did not state it explicitly.

I say: For this reason, Allah knows best, some of the later exegetes said: The closer view is that this beast is a speaking human being who debates the people of innovation and disbelief and argues with them so that they are silenced, so that whoever perishes perishes by clear evidence, and whoever lives lives by clear evidence. Our shaykh, the Imam Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Umar al-Qurtubi, said in his book al-Mufhim: The reason this speaker held the view that it is closer is His saying, the Exalted: "it will speak to them." On this view, there is no extraordinary sign specific to this beast, and it would not be among the ten signs mentioned in the hadith, because the existence of debaters and those who argue against the people of innovation is common, so there is no sign specific to it, and it should not be mentioned with the ten. Its unique existence is also lifted when the word is fulfilled. Moreover, it involves a departure from naming this virtuous, learned debater, whom the people of the earth should call a human, a scholar, or an imam, by the name of a beast. This is a departure from the custom of eloquent speakers and from the honouring of scholars, and it is not the practice of sensible people. So the better view is what the people of tafsir have said, and Allah knows best the realities of matters.

I say: The difficulty concerning this beast has been removed by what we have mentioned from the hadith of Hudhayfah, so let it be relied upon. It has been disputed from which place it will emerge. Abdullah ibn Umar said: It will emerge from Mount Safa in Makkah, splitting open, and it will come out of it. Abdullah ibn Amr said something similar and said: "If I wished to place my foot upon the place of its emergence, I would do so." It was also reported in a report from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The earth will split open for the beast, while Isa, peace be upon him, is circling the House, and with him are the Muslims from the direction of al-Masa'. It is also mentioned in the report that it has fur and feathers, as al-Mahdawi mentioned.

Al-Zamakhshari said: it will emerge from between the Corner, opposite the house of Banu Makhzum, on the right of one leaving the mosque. Some people will flee, and some will stand watching.

It was reported from Qatadah that it will emerge in Tihamah. It was also reported that it will emerge from the mosque of Kufah, from the place where the oven of Nuh, peace be upon him, boiled over. It was also said: from the land of al-Ta'if. Abu Qabil said: Abdullah ibn Amr struck the land of al-Ta'if with his foot and said: "From here the beast will emerge which speaks to the people." It was also said: from some valleys of Tihamah, said by Ibn Abbas. It was said: from a rock in the valley of Ajyad, said by Abdullah ibn Amr. It was said: from the Sea of Sodom (Sadum), said by Wahb ibn Munabbih. Al-Mawardi mentioned these last three sayings in his book.

Al-Baghawi Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz mentioned: Ali ibn al-Ja'd narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq al-Raqqashi al-Aghar (about whom Yahya ibn Ma'in was asked, and he said: "trustworthy"), from Atiyyah al-Awfi, from Ibn Umar, who said: "The beast will emerge from a crack in the Ka'bah, running like a horse for three days, and a third of it will not emerge."

I say: These are the sayings of the Companions and the Successor regarding the emergence of the beast and its description. They refute the view of those exegetes who said that the beast is merely a speaking human being who debates the people of innovation and disbelief. Abu Umamah narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The beast will emerge and mark people on their noses." This was mentioned by al-Mawardi.
